description:
A giant snake with a long, low brown-and-tan body and pale underside. The original template has no carried gear or wealth. Its saved combat footprint is two squares wide and one square high; the ready body must visibly span both squares, while the action head lunges right to bite from the same grounded body.

Image 1 is the existing independently generated giant-snake ready art, used ONLY as the identity and palette reference: brown and tan mottled scales, pale underside, broad predatory head, red forked tongue. Redesign its POSE to fill the saved TWO-SQUARE-WIDE, ONE-SQUARE-HIGH combat footprint. On the final 128 x 128 canvas, the snake's low continuous body should span roughly x=8 through x=110 (about 100 pixels of horizontal visible length), with its resting belly/coil base near y=113, and its raised head no higher than y=65. The tail and long thick body occupy the LEFT square; a low S-shaped coil crosses into the RIGHT square and leads naturally to the head at the RIGHT edge. The head faces screen right, alert and poised to bite, mouth mostly closed. Preserve generous transparent margin, especially to the right for the later bite. Make the snake clearly ONE continuous animal: follow the spine/scale pattern smoothly from tail through body, neck, and head. Keep it LOW: no upright cobra coil, no body taller than one combat square. Plan the pair at one fixed scale; the later action will keep the entire body/coil and ground anchor unchanged while only the head and short neck reach right and open to bite. Crisp hand-painted pixel art readable at combat size, genuine transparent background; no ground plane, scenery, border, text, weapon, limbs, duplicate heads, opaque black box, alpha halo, or sprite sheet. Output only the ready frame.
